The Muslims' span beside earlier nations is like Asr to sunset; in parables of hired labourers, the Torah and Gospel people worked longer, yet the Muslims earned double.
Eating fresh dates, the Prophet says one tree resembles a faithful believer; Ibn Umar, the youngest present, kept quiet, and the Prophet names the date palm.
Muslims, Jews and Christians are like labourers hired for parts of a day; the Muslims, working from Asr to sunset, get double pay, which Allah calls His blessing.
Labourers who quit at midday and at Asr forfeit their wages, while a last batch working till sunset receives both batches' wages; such are the Muslims, who accepted the guidance.
Those who keep Allah's limits and those who break them are like people in a boat: if the upper deck stops the lower from holing it, all are saved.
Those keeping Allah's limits and those violating them are like people in a boat: stopping one who holes its bottom saves everyone, while leaving him destroys all.
Ibn Abbas called the verse of the garden a parable for deeds; Umar explained it as a rich man whose good deeds are lost when Satan leads him into sin.
The Prophet asked about a tree like a Muslim whose leaves never fall; Ibn Umar thought of the date palm but kept quiet, and Umar wished he had spoken.
A believer reciting the Quran is like a citron and a wicked reciter like basil; Muslims working from Asr to sunset earn twice the wage of Jews and Christians.
A believer who recites the Quran and acts on it is like a citron, and a hypocrite who recites it is like basil, sweet-smelling but bitter.
The Prophet likened himself to a warner of an approaching army whom some believed and were saved, and to a man holding back moths rushing into a fire.
